title: Teach You a Lesson Ending Explained — Who Killed Ga-yun?
excerpt: Netflix's #1 K-drama in 85 countries ends on a partial victory. The murder, the drug network, and why Hwa-jin doesn't pull the trigger.
author: StarScoop Daily Staff
imageAlt: Teach You a Lesson Netflix K-drama backdrop — ending explained
metaDescription: Teach You a Lesson ending explained — who killed Ga-yun, how the bureau exposes the drug network, and what the final school scene means.
content:
Spoilers for the full season of Teach You a Lesson.

The short version: Gyu-cheol killed Ga-yun, and Hwa-jin chooses to arrest him rather than kill him. That restraint is the entire point of the ending.

DetailInfo
PlatformNetflix
Episodes10 · complete
StarringKim Moo-yul, Lee Sung-min, Jin Ki-joo, Pyo Ji-hoon
TMDB rating4.7 / 5
SourceBased on the webtoon Get Schooled

What the Show Is

An inspector from the Educational Rights Protection Bureau is authorized by the government to use physical intervention and unconventional methods to discipline delinquent students and reform the school system.

It is a revenge fantasy, and it knows it. The premise exists because Korean schools have a real and heavily reported problem with bullying that institutions have repeatedly failed to solve.

The show has topped Netflix's non-English chart across 85 countries since June, and holds a 4.7/5 on TMDB — an unusually high score.

Who Killed Ga-yun, and Why

This is the question the whole season is built around, and the answer reframes everything.

Ga-yun was Hwa-jin's fiancée. She was also Gang-seok's daughter — which means the case is personal for two of the central characters, not one.

She was a teacher trying to guide Gyu-cheol back into school. In doing so she discovered his drug activity. When she confronted him about it, he killed her.

So Hwa-jin's entire crusade — the bureau, the violence, the willingness to operate outside the rules — traces back to a woman who tried to help a student and died for it. That reframes his methods as grief rather than ideology.

How the Bureau Wins

The final act works because it inverts the show's own formula.

Official channels get deliberately slowed, attacked and pressured — the bureau is politically squeezed and effectively shut down. So the team goes rogue, and Hwa-jin uses the shutdown and the public backlash as cover to expose Gyu-cheol's wider drug operation.

The crucial detail is who actually does the work. Teachers from schools across Seoul — the people the bureau had protected earlier in the season — quietly band together, collect the hidden drugs, and assemble hard evidence against the syndicate.

That is the show paying off its own premise. For nine episodes one man punches the problem. In the finale, the people he defended solve it themselves.

Gyu-cheol is arrested. Hwa-jin, standing in front of the man who murdered his fiancée, chooses justice over killing him.

The Final Scene Explained

The closing beat is at Kangju High School, and it's easy to misread as a joke.

Geun-de arrives dressed like Hwa-jin and tries to teach a bully a lesson himself. Han-rim shows up and joins him. Both of them struggle badly against the bully — until Hwa-jin arrives to help.

It plays as comedy. It isn't only comedy.

Two people who were protected earlier now try to protect someone else, and discover it is genuinely hard. The bureau's real legacy isn't the arrests — it's that other people started trying.

Why the Ending Is Deliberately Incomplete

This is a partial victory, and the restraint is the most interesting choice in the show.

The bureau exposes the final crime and survives the political attack. But nothing is fixed. The series does not pretend every school, every parent or every institution has been repaired.

A revenge fantasy usually ends with the villain destroyed and the world corrected. This one ends with one man punished and the work explicitly ongoing.

The honest criticism: a show this angry about institutional failure arguably has it both ways — it spends nine episodes enjoying the violence it spends the finale rejecting. Whether that reads as maturity or as having its cake depends on how much you trust the last twenty minutes.

Is There a Season 2?

Netflix lists the series as Ended after one 10-episode season, and no renewal has been announced.

The finale is structured to allow one — the bureau survives, the work is unfinished, and the source webtoon has more material. But an announcement is a different thing from an opening, and none has come.

Anyone telling you a second season is confirmed is guessing.
